methods.name: computer.permissions
methods.resultContract: Path resolution: env override (existence-checked) -> packaged path -> 2 dev candidates -> null; executable path is a second independent existsSync check inside the resolved bundle. --agent requires non-empty --token-file or exits 2; bare invocation with no matching flag exits 13 via runStdio(). Per-request server-side token re-validation (permission_denied on mismatch) plus a separate authorizedPeer gate, both confirmed new findings not in prior reports.

methods.name: computer.permissionsStatus
methods.resultContract: writePermissionStatus atomically writes {accessibility,screenshots} granted/not-granted JSON to the given path; write failure exits 1. Probe runs accessibility+screenshot checks CONCURRENTLY on a shared DispatchQueue joined via a blocking DispatchGroup.wait() -- no partial result shape, both must complete. PermissionStatusRefreshCoordinator coalesces concurrent refresh() calls via a locked refreshInFlight boolean -- a second concurrent refresh is a silent no-op, not queued.

methods.name: computer.listWindows
methods.resultContract: Linux: windowId targeting always throws (unsupported by AT-SPI provider); window.id always null; screenIndex always null; window selection fallback order ACTIVE -> SHOWING -> first-in-AT-SPI-order. Windows: hard single-window-per-process model, Assert-OrcaWindowTarget throws windowNotFound for any windowIndex!=0 or windowId!=MainWindowHandle; windowId is the real MainWindowHandle value (not null like Linux).

methods.name: computer.getAppState
methods.resultContract: Cross-platform cache parity confirmed: TS store and native macOS cache both use 32-entry/2-minute FIFO policy, identical stale-alias-safe eviction, identical namespace/case-sensitivity rules. Screenshot payload always stripped before caching (both TS and native macOS). TS rendering layer hardcodes window.isMinimized/isOffscreen/screenIndex to null regardless of native list_windows-only fields; focusedElementId defensively re-validated against the elements array; screenshotStatus.captured.metadata.engine is always the literal 'unknown'.

keyNewFindings.crossPlatformWindowChangedRetryParity: All three native producers (Linux, Windows, macOS) independently implement the identical window-disappeared-mid-action retry: on window_not_found/window_stale with an explicit window selector, retry unscoped and force verification={state:unverified,reason:window_changed}.
keyNewFindings.crossPlatformSnapshotCacheParity: TS DesktopScriptSnapshotStore and native macOS Provider cache both use 32-entry/2-minute FIFO with identical stale-alias-safe eviction and namespace rules, independently implemented in TypeScript and Swift.
keyNewFindings.macosPerRequestTokenRevalidationAndPeerA: handleRequest re-validates the request token per-call (not just at socket-connect time) and additionally requires a separate authorizedPeer (unix-socket peer-credential) check; both throw permission_denied on failure. Not characterized in any prior report.
keyNewFindings.macosHelperCliExitCodes: Distinct exit codes confirmed: 13 (runStdio, no matching CLI flag), 2 (--agent with missing/empty token file), 1 (writePermissionStatus file-write failure).
keyNewFindings.windowsSingleWindowCeiling: Windows Assert-OrcaWindowTarget throws windowNotFound for any windowIndex other than 0 or any windowId other than the process's actual MainWindowHandle -- a hard single-window-per-process model, unlike Linux/macOS multi-window enumeration.
keyNewFindings.linuxWindowIdUnsupported: Linux always throws for windowId targeting ('use windowIndex'); window.id is always null in Linux's own window_json.
keyNewFindings.linuxWindowsBlockedAppListingAsymmetry: Blocked-app (password manager) filtering is enforced only when resolving a single target app for actions/snapshot, NOT when listing all apps -- a blocked app still appears in computer.listApps on both Linux and Windows.
keyNewFindings.setValueVerificationIsTsBridgeOnly: Neither Linux nor Windows native scripts implement a value_mismatch partial-success verification shape; that enrichment is TS-bridge-layer only (desktop-script-action.ts), wrapping a native binary settable/not-settable outcome.
keyNewFindings.pasteClipboardRestoreParity: Both Linux and Windows independently save/restore the pre-existing clipboard around paste, and both explicitly clear the clipboard afterward if there was no prior value to restore -- neither leaves agent-provided paste text sitting in the system clipboard.
